newsitem.title: USA: Applied Cellular sees acquisition gains.
newsitem.headline: Applied Cellular sees acquisition gains.

text.p: Applied Cellular Technology Inc said Monday it has finalized its acquisition agreement with ATI Communications Inc of Bethel Park, Pa., and expects an increase in sales revenues from the combination.
An acquisition agreement had been entered into on June 12, 1996. Terms of the acquisition were not disclosed.
ATI Communications is a privately held supplier of interconnect and cellular phone equipment. ATI also operates a domestic long distance carrier service.
The acquisition will have an effective accounting date of August 31, 1996.

ATI estimates its sales for 1996 will approach $32.5 million. Sales for 1997 are estimated at $39 million. The company is currently expanding its interconnect services and plans to expand its new long distance carrier services, which could increase revenues in 1997 exponentially, Applied Cellular said in a statement.

Applied Cellular said it expects the acquisition will increase Applied Cellular's total annualized sales revenues over the next 12 months in excess of an estimated $48 million level, or a 350 percent increase over the current rate of $10.5 million.
"This acquisition will enable the company to achieve tremendous cross-marketing opportunities," said Richard Sullivan, chairman of Applied Cellular, in a statement.

"We anticipate that due to the strong national marketing capabilities already established by ATI, that the combined sales of our technical wireless data applications and software products with ATI's cellular product lines and interconnect services will result in dramatic sales growth opportunities," he said.
Applied Cellular is a computer technology company specializing in wireless cellular technologies.
